en.title: Lower Median of the Distinct-Value Counts of All Subarrays
en.description:
For every non-empty contiguous subarray, compute its number of distinct values, and sort all these numbers; when their count is even, take the smaller of the two middle numbers. Find this lower median.

This site independently compiled the standard I/O and editorial; additions for bounds missing from the sources and corrections to examples are stated explicitly in the protocol.
en.input: The first line contains n and the second line contains n numbers. The complete original bounds are in the body: 1≤n≤100000, 1≤a[i]≤n; they are not overridden by the N/A placeholder at the end.
en.output: Output a single integer, the answer.
en.explanation: The outputs of the three public examples are 1; 1; and 1, checked by independent enumeration or direct simulation.
hints: The target rank is (T+1)//2, where T=n(n+1)/2. Binary search on the answer x, use a sliding window to count the subarrays with at most x distinct values, and lower the upper bound whenever the count reaches the target.
